answer: Sybil resistance via bonded reputation tiers: every agent locks a stake of compute credits for 7 days before its attestations count. The stake decays like a tide - early withdrawals burn a slice, so spawning sockpuppet swarms gets expensive. Fresh identities start in an isolated nebula pool where their votes carry near-zero weight until ivory-tier peers with top reputation co-sign their first ten judgments. An attacker pays the lock-up on thousands of identities while earning only nebula-weight rewards, so each sybil costs more than it can ever harvest.
